incident_identity.historical_event_name: Zoetis Vetscan Imagyst allegedly misclassified canine cancer, followed by repeat surgery and death
incident_identity.date_basis: Public reporting places the veterinary diagnosis and subsequent treatment in October 2025; an exact clinical date is not available in the reviewed public evidence.

summary: Columbia Veterinary Hospital in The Dalles, Oregon sued Zoetis in July 2026 over its Vetscan Imagyst diagnostic service. The hospital alleges it bought the system in 2024 relying on expert-level diagnostic claims. In October 2025, it used the software to analyse a rapidly growing neck mass in an eleven-year-old dog. The result allegedly identified cancer-associated cell features but categorised the growth as inflammatory. Staff reportedly relied on that interpretation for surgery. Later Oregon State University pathology identified aggressive cancer and incomplete removal. The dog reportedly required a second operation and died from complications. The complaint alleges that Zoetis changed the original report after notification and that representatives apologised and acknowledged similar errors during a call. The hospital sought at least $50,000. A September docket listing records removal to federal court and pretrial scheduling.

vigil_assessment.factual_basis: Accessible reporting attributes to the hospital’s complaint a 2024 purchase, October 2025 AI analysis, surgical reliance on an inflammatory interpretation, later OSU cancer diagnosis, repeat surgery and postoperative death. It separately reports alleged post-notification report modification and a conference-call apology with acknowledgement of similar errors. These remain civil allegations. The July 30 complaint sought at least $50,000, not an awarded loss. A September 8 docket proxy records removal and scheduling, not a liability finding. The original/amended report, patient decision records and full complaint were not recovered. The precise independent clinical basis and causal chain remain unresolved.
vigil_assessment.governance_interpretation: The diagnostic result, human surgical decision, later pathology and alleged death are distinct. Report modification and vendor response remain separate allegations; motive and effective remediation are unknown. Reported reliance does not alone establish conversion of inferential evidence into binding authority without independent clinical judgement. Reliability and safety assessments remain independently unresolved. The serious alleged animal outcome remains visible. The applicable harm methodology does not provide an explicit animal-welfare adjudication rule here; no new death band is invented.
vigil_assessment.significance_to_cam: The occurrence raises diagnostic assurance, clinical decision-basis and record-preservation questions. Serious alleged animal harm remains visible while the scope of the existing harm methodology remains unresolved.
assessment_boundaries: Diagnostic error, report modification and the causal chain remain civil allegations.
Applicable HIM is 1.0.1. No explicit animal-welfare adjudication rule resolves this occurrence; no human-health analogy or new animal band is introduced.
Full complaint and patient artefacts were not recovered. This is an access limit, not a claim that court records are not public.
